packageRules.description: Aurelia moves as one unit. No upstream group covers it — `aurelia` and the `@aurelia/*` packages publish from the same release train and mixing versions across them is not supported. Storybook, Vitest, OpenTelemetry JS, stylelint, Vite and workbox are deliberately NOT re-grouped here: maintained upstream presets already cover them, and a local copy would not learn about packages added to those families later. The observation phase checks that assumption before any of them automerges.

The liverty-music schema SDK is advanced by the OpenSpec change that alters the schema, together with the code migration that change requires. `enabled: false` rather than `ignoreDeps` keeps it visible on the dependency dashboard, so a schema release whose consumers were never advanced is detectable. See design D7.

NEVER automerge @playwright/test. A version bump changes Chromium's rendering and therefore invalidates every committed toMatchScreenshot baseline, which Renovate cannot regenerate — CI goes red and stays red until a human regenerates them inside the pinned container. The package version, the CI container tag and the tag in the documented regeneration command must also move together; see the custom manager binding them.

Do NOT let the github-actions manager propose the Playwright CI container on its own. The `container: image:` in .github/workflows/ci.yaml is ALSO detected by that manager as a plain docker dependency, which opened a second branch (`renovate/mcr.microsoft.com-playwright-1.x`) that moves the container tag without the package — and, being a github-actions minor, it fell under the organization's stage 1 automerge. The custom manager below already moves this tag together with @playwright/test inside the `playwright` group, so this path adds nothing but a way to split them. Matching `datasource: docker` leaves the custom manager's dependency (`@playwright/test` on the npm datasource) untouched.

NEVER automerge vite-plugin-pwa. Its surface has two halves and CI covers only one. The caching half is covered — the `pwa` Playwright project runs against a production build and asserts the service worker activates, controls the page and precaches the app shell. The manifest / install-prompt half is not: `pwa-install-prompt.spec.ts` cannot run in CI because `beforeinstallprompt` depends on browser install heuristics, and it is an enumerated gap in docs/ci-coverage-gaps.md with no compensating control. Do NOT resolve this by routing the pull request to a human instead — a reviewer sees a version number and a lock file and cannot evaluate install-prompt behaviour any better than the pipeline can. It stays proposed-but-unmerged until that gap has a control. Note this package is a devDependency, so without this rule the organization preset's devDependencies automerge would carry it. See change task 10.4c.

NEVER automerge an npm `overrides` entry. These encode a human judgement about a transitive advisory, and their correct resolution is often REMOVAL rather than upgrade — `fflate` and `dompurify` are both pinned because posthog-js caps them, and they go away when posthog-js widens its ranges. Renovate can raise the version inside an override but cannot decide the override should cease to exist.

customManagers.description: Bind the two mcr.microsoft.com/playwright image tags to @playwright/test. This is the ONLY custom manager in this project, and it exists because the third location is prose: frontend/AGENTS.md documents the baseline-regeneration command with the same tag, and no tool derives a version from a contributor document. Go and Node duplication was removed by deriving from go.mod / .nvmrc instead — see design D4. If a way to derive this one appears, delete this manager rather than maintaining it. A mismatch here is not cosmetic: a human following AGENTS.md would regenerate committed visual baselines against a different renderer than the one CI validates them with, silently poisoning the PNGs.
